amendments.body: The test does not assert DO (dissolved oxygen) or alkalinity per-liter deltas after the tick. Nitrification consumes O2 and alkalinity via fixed stoichiometric factors (o2_for_aob=3.43, o2_for_nob=1.14, etc.), so these are derived from the N deltas. However, a volume-dependent bug in the DO/alkalinity bookkeeping code path (lines 230-235, 288-289, 332-334, 362-364 of nitrogen_cycle.rs) would not be caught. Add assertions for DO and alkalinity per-liter deltas alongside the existing TAN/NO2/NO3/DOC/DON checks to close this gap.
amendments.rationale: The acceptance criteria and backlog comment say: 'Assert both the Monod factor AND the per-liter concentration delta. A test that only checks the factor could miss volume leaks in the rate-to-mass conversion step.' DO and alkalinity undergo their own rate-to-mass conversion within step_nitrogen_cycle and are thus subject to the same class of volume leak. The stoichiometric relationship only holds if the O2/alk debits are computed from the same oxidized_n_mg values — a separate bug (e.g., accidentally using total DO instead of budget) in that conversion would not propagate to the N-species deltas.

amendments.body: The extreme-scale test (concentration_kinetics_volume_independent_extreme_scales) does not include the Monod factor verification section that the primary test has. While the per-liter delta check is the stronger assertion, the acceptance criteria call for verifying Monod factors specifically. Add the same Monod factor comparison block (or factor it into a shared helper) so both tests cover both criteria.
amendments.rationale: The extreme-scale test omits the explicit Monod factor assertions present in the primary test. If a future change introduces a volume-dependent K (half-saturation) parameter that only manifests at extreme scale ratios (e.g., due to floating-point precision in legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l), this gap would let it slip through.

payload.summary: The two regression tests (concentration_kinetics_are_volume_independent and concentration_kinetics_volume_independent_extreme_scales) are well-designed, thorough, and correctly verify the acceptance criteria. Both tests pass. The setup carefully isolates nitrogen kinetics by zeroing growth/decay, disabling non-nitrogen systems, and scaling biomass + dissolved species proportionally to volume. Monod factor equality, per-liter concentration deltas (TAN, NO2, NO3, DOC, DON), and non-zero sanity checks are all verified. The extreme-scale test (1L vs 1000L) adds value for floating-point edge cases. Two minor coverage gaps identified: (1) DO/alkalinity deltas are not asserted, and (2) the extreme-scale test omits Monod factor verification.
